explain.say: Have you ever said, "I am bored!" and flopped on the sofa? Boredom feels flat and itchy at the same time. But it might be trying to tell you something! Look at the question on the board.

groups.ask: What can I do when I am bored?

faq.a: Boredom is the flat, restless feeling you get when nothing interests you or keeps your brain busy. It is your brain asking for something new or meaningful to do.

faq.q: Why do I get bored at school?
faq.a: Work that is too easy or too hard, sitting still for a long time, or not seeing why a topic matters can all feel boring. Telling your teacher can help them find a better fit.
asks: Why are some lessons so boring?

faq.q: Is being bored good for you?
faq.a: A bit of boredom can be good. It gives your mind space to daydream, which can lead to creative ideas and new hobbies.

faq.q: What can I do when I am bored?
faq.a: Make something, like a drawing or a den; move your body; help someone at home; or read, daydream and watch the world. Keep a list of ideas for bored moments.
asks: I am bored, what should I do?

faq.q: Why do I reach for a screen when I am bored?
faq.a: Screens give a quick, easy fix for boredom. That is fine sometimes, but trying something else first can lead to more fun and new ideas.
asks: Why do I always want my tablet when bored?

facts: In a 2014 study in the UK, people who first did a boring task, copying phone numbers, came up with more creative ideas afterwards.
The word boredom became popular in English in the 1800s, and Charles Dickens used it in his novel Bleak House, published in 1852 and 1853.
